feature_notes:
Adds usable openpyxl-compatible scalar read_only and write_only modes over bounded canonical Rust streams. Read-only values stream without editable worksheet models; write-only sheets accept interleaved append calls and spool XML to disk. Supports temporal values and supported normal/array/data-table formulas, independent iterators, one-shot saves and deterministic close/abort/failure cleanup.

Fixes Python read performance by batching ordinary values conversion by row and returning streaming scalar values directly. Verified Linux CPython 3.12 measurements for one million numeric cells: ordinary complete read/consume improves from alpha.1 3.08 seconds to 1.34 seconds; read_only is 0.80 seconds and write_only is 1.73 seconds, with streaming peak RSS around 18 MiB. Python-calamine remains faster for reading this workload (0.52 seconds); these measurements do not claim complete feature parity or isolate the XML upgrade. Numeric write-only spool peak is about 31.3 MiB plus the transient final ZIP. See benchmarks/optimized-modes.md for raw evidence and Unicode workloads.

Pins canonical Rust alpha.2 commit 6d617a48cf5a134d2d8b09a83cbf642970d4e613, including quick-xml 0.42.0, interleaved spools, bounded prefix reads and Windows same-path save fixes. Core MSRV is Rust 1.88; Python compilation uses latest stable Rust, and source builds require Rust 1.99 or newer. Prebuilt wheel users do not need Rust.

Packages CPython 3.11 through 3.15 (currently RC): Linux x86_64/ARM64, Windows x86_64, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon. All 25 installed wheel test combinations and the independent sdist test must pass before OIDC publication; the selected suite has 577 tests.

Complete optimized-mode style/rich-text objects, write-only reordering/random access, column-wise read-only iteration, file-like I/O and advanced baseline features remain staged and raise explicit unsupported errors. Row bounds, including declared dimensions, skip unread worksheet XML/CRC; reset dimensions for unbounded full validation. Component allowances are not a process RSS cap.
